clue.text: What's on this disc isn't 14's cup of tea

definitions.text: What's on this disc isn't 14's cup of tea

parts.words: What's on this disc isn't 14's cup of tea
parts.note: a small cardboard disc set under a pint in a pub carries a drink that a teetotaller (the solver of 14) would refuse

explanation.surface: A remark that whatever is on some disc does not suit the taste of the person at 14 across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup of tea' reads as a drink, but here it is the idiom for something you like; the disc sits under a glass of beer, which the abstainer at 14 avoids.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub coaster made of card, printed with a brewery's logo, is placed under a glass of ale.

clue.text: Black bird put in biologist's vessel

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a large bird of prey

explanation.surface: A dark bird is placed inside a scientist's container in the lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a flask in a lab; it is the ship on which Charles Darwin sailed round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Beagle was the ship that carried the naturalist Charles Darwin on his voyage.

clue.text: Artist in college unfortunately one left out without right

indicators.note: without means outside, so the jumbled letters sit around the other piece
unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
out says the piece named just before it is left off the word college

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left; one left means a single L

explanation.surface: An art student at college is sadly missing someone who has left, lacking any guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops one L from COLLEGE, leaving COLEGE; 'unfortunately' rearranges that to ELGECO, and 'without' wraps it round R. 'Without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan-born painter Domenikos Theotokopoulos worked in Toledo and is known by this Spanish nickname meaning 'the Greek'.

clue.text: The drink takes a lot out of fish

parts.note: to milk someone is to exploit them, taking as much from them as possible
the hake is a sea fish related to the cod

explanation.surface: Drinking exhausts a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes a lot out of' looks like tiredness, but it is a phrase for exploiting, giving MILKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A frothy beverage of milk blended with ice cream or flavouring.

clue.text: Tutors ignoring one mother? That's clear

indicators.note: ignoring means the named letter is left out of the word before it

parts.note: to train someone is to tutor or coach them
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mother is one kind of parent

explanation.surface: Teachers paying no attention to a mum makes things obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something see-through, or easy to understand, is clear.

clue.text: Transport for a few reduced in rank?

definitions.text: Transport for a few reduced in rank?

parts.words: Transport for a few reduced in rank?
parts.note: read as a small hired car for a handful of passengers, a smaller version of a taxi that waits on a rank

explanation.surface: Asking whether a vehicle for a small party has been demoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced in rank' sounds like a demotion; the rank is a taxi rank, and 'reduced' points to a small cab.
explanation.definitionFit: A small taxi that must be booked by phone carries a few passengers.

clue.text: Girl, one embraced by me?

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A girl who gets a hug from the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A female forename, as for the film star Mae West.

clue.text: Impractical idea one's spurned

indicators.note: spurned means rejected, so the letter for one is thrown out

parts.note: a notion is an idea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone's unworkable idea is rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impractical idea' looks like the definition as a whole; only 'Impractical' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'not on' describes a plan that cannot be done or is unacceptable.

clue.text: Top soldiers once elected one of their officers?

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
TA is the Territorial Army, the former name of Britain's volunteer reserve force
a candidate voted in is elected

explanation.surface: Senior troops once chose a leader from among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to soldiers: a captain is an army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An army officer ranked above a lieutenant and below a major.

clue.text: Poet with funny yarn set in farm location

indicators.note: set in means placed inside the poet word

parts.note: a bard is a poet

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of yarn are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet with an odd story sets it on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' looks like it describes the story, but it signals the jumble RNYA, which 'set in' puts inside the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The enclosed yard around a farm's outbuildings.

clue.text: Item of confectionery, article set to become hard

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a jelly that sets is said to gel
to cake is to harden into a crust

explanation.surface: A piece of a sweet item is about to harden.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, airy sponge made with egg whites is a sweet baked treat.

clue.text: Light exercises accepted by sailor

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the following word

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A sailor agrees to some gentle physical training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective for the exercises; it is a noun, a slender candle.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin candle or wax-coated wick used to light other flames.

clue.text: City connections mentioned on the radio

indicators.note: something spoken on the radio is heard, not seen, so this signals a word that sounds the same

parts.note: leads are cables connecting equipment

explanation.surface: A city's links get talked about on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in West Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Sitting down? Tray needs to be repositioned

indicators.note: repositioned means moved about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tray must be moved before someone takes a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk-bound life spent seated is inactive, involving much sitting.

clue.text: Toe sprained badly, in a terrible state

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A badly twisted toe leaves someone in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopelessness so deep that one would try anything is a dreadful condition.

clue.text: Who'd find cracking a bottle a strain?

definitions.text: Who'd find cracking a bottle a strain?

parts.words: Who'd find cracking a bottle a strain?
parts.note: read as someone for whom opening a bottle of drink is an ordeal because they never touch alcohol

explanation.surface: Asking who struggles to open a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking a bottle' sounds like breaking glass; it is the idiom for opening a drink. 'A strain' puns on 'abstain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who never drinks alcohol at all would find opening a bottle uncomfortable.

clue.text: One appears to be in a stupor, if on it

definitions.text: One appears to be in a stupor, if on it

parts.words: One appears to be in a stupor, if on it
parts.note: read as a pilot who lets an automatic flying system steer seems dazed; 'on it' also means acting without thought

explanation.surface: Someone who seems dazed when engaged in something.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'on autopilot' is an idiom for doing things mechanically without attention, so the person seems in a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: The automatic steering system of an aircraft; a person said to be on it acts without thinking.

clue.text: One looks forward to experiencing their views

definitions.text: One looks forward to experiencing their views

parts.words: One looks forward to experiencing their views
parts.note: read as people whose visions look forward in time, foretelling the future

explanation.surface: Someone eager to hear certain people's opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks forward to' sounds like eager anticipation; it is literal, as clairvoyants claim to see the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Clairvoyants and mediums claim to foresee events, so their visions look ahead.

clue.text: Shopper?

parts.note: read as one who shops in the slang sense, informing on thieves to the police

explanation.walkthrough: To 'shop' someone is British slang for reporting them to the police, so a shopper turns in shoplifters.
explanation.definitionFit: A security officer in a department store catches thieves and hands them over to police.

clue.text: Weight problem to follow, limiting occupancy of chair

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the word for to follow surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to obey is to follow orders
to sit is to occupy a chair

explanation.surface: A heavy issue comes next, keeping someone from sitting down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being severely overweight is a medical concern about body mass.

clue.text: Three people engaged in a lot of nasty harsh criticism

indicators.note: engaged in means placed inside the next piece
a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: vile means nasty
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: Three people get caught up in much unpleasant, cruel abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of nasty' trims the synonym to VIL; 'engaged in' looks like a betrothal but puts the group of three inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally sulphuric acid, figuratively bitter, caustic abuse in speech or writing.

clue.text: Believe it allows you to drink for free today?

definitions.meaning: to ... a story is to believe it

definitions.text: it allows you to drink for free today?
definitions.meaning: a tab at the bar lets you drink now without paying until later

explanation.surface: A drinker asks whether some arrangement lets them drink for nothing today.
explanation.definitionFit: To give credence is to trust; a deferred-payment arrangement means no cash changes hands now.

clue.text: Lo! Ace part in play!

indicators.note: in play means put into motion, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An excited cry at landing a great role in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the queen of Egypt is a star part in Shakespeare's 'Antony and Cleopatra'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title role of a Shakespeare tragedy is a prized acting part.

clue.text: Ancient city favoured by artist

parts.note: a pet is a favoured one, as in teacher's pet
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An old city preferred by a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock-cut Nabataean city in Jordan dates from antiquity.

clue.text: Father lacking a time for glib speech

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: patter is fast, smooth talk
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A dad without the time for smooth talk.
explanation.walkthrough: PATTER has two Ts; 'lacking a time' drops just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for a male parent, used in old-fashioned British slang for one's dad.

clue.text: Fool? One's one in a spot

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in means the second numeral is placed inside the spot

parts.note: a dot is a small spot
I again, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are being foolish, being the one in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a spot' reads as in trouble; here it puts I into DOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person is a fool.

clue.text: Storm endlessly to lash both sides, with twisting motion

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is removed

parts.note: to whip is to lash
right and left are both sides, abbreviated R and L
a wind is a twist or turn, as of a road

explanation.surface: A gale that beats both flanks with a whirling movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts WHIP to WHI. 'With twisting motion' looks like part of the definition, but 'with' is the link and 'twisting motion' gives WIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating column of air is a kind of tempest.

clue.text: Pan beginning to work satisfactorily

indicators.note: beginning to means take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: OK means satisfactorily, all right

explanation.surface: A cooking pan starting to perform adequately.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl-shaped Chinese frying vessel.

clue.text: Bird, game associated with Scottish island, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
a lark is a game or prank

explanation.surface: A bird and a game linked with a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' and 'game' both hint at birds shot for sport; 'game' here is a bit of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird famous for singing while it hovers high up.

clue.text: Lease arranged offline, say, in short communication

parts.note: a paper note is one example of an offline, non-electronic message; read also as NOT E, not electronic
to let is to lease; a property let is one whose lease is arranged

explanation.surface: A rental agreement fixed without the internet, in a brief message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the phrase for LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folded card or sheet for a brief letter is a short message.
